questions.text: Ram and Shyam have been asked to show that a certain problem $\Pi$ is NP-complete. Ram shows a polynomial time reduction from the 3-SAT problem to $\Pi$, and Shyam shows a polynomial time reduction from $\Pi$ to 3-SAT. Which of the following can be inferred from these reductions?

questions.text: Let $(S, \leq)$ be a partial order with two minimal elements $a$ and $b$, and a maximum element $c$. Let $P : S \rightarrow \{\text{True}, \text{False}\}$ be a predicate defined on $S$. Suppose that $P(a) = \text{True}$, $P(b) = \text{False}$ and $P(x) \Rightarrow P(y)$ for all $x, y \in S$ satisfying $x \leq y$, where $\Rightarrow$ stands for logical implication. Which of the following statements CANNOT be true?
questions.optA: $P(x) = \text{True}$ for all $x \in S$ such that $x \neq b$
questions.optB: $P(x) = \text{False}$ for all $x \in S$ such that $x \neq a$ and $x \neq c$
questions.optC: $P(x) = \text{False}$ for all $x \in S$ such that $b \leq x$ such that $x \neq c$
questions.optD: $P(x) = \text{False}$ for all $x \in S$ such that $a \leq x$ and $b \leq x$
questions.subject: 1. Discrete Maths
questions.referenceAnswer: Since a is below the maximum c, monotonicity forces P(c)=True. But c is above both a and b, so D would force P(c)=False. The other descriptions can hold for suitable posets and predicates.

questions.text: Which of the following is a valid first order formula? (Here $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are first order formulae with $x$ as their only free variable)
questions.subject: 1. Discrete Maths
questions.referenceAnswer: If every x satisfies alpha implies beta and every x satisfies alpha, then each x satisfies beta. This proves D by universal instantiation, modus ponens and generalization. A incorrectly derives pointwise implication from an implication between two universal statements.

questions.text: Consider the following formula $\alpha$ and its two interpretations $I_1$ and $I_2$. $\alpha : (\forall x) [P_x \Leftrightarrow (\forall y) [Q_{xy} \Leftrightarrow \neg Q_{yy}]] \Rightarrow (\forall x) [\neg P_x]$. $I_1 :$ Domain : the set of natural numbers, $P_x =$ 'x is a prime number', $Q_{xy} =$ 'y divides x'. $I_2 :$ Same as $I_1$ except that $P_x =$ 'x is a composite number.' Which of the following statements is true?
questions.subject: 1. Discrete Maths
questions.referenceAnswer: Take y=x in the inner universal equivalence. Q(x,x) iff not Q(x,x) is false. Thus its universal quantification is false for every x. The antecedent would require every P(x) to be false, but both interpretations have a prime or a composite. Its antecedent is false, so the whole implication is true in both interpretations.

questions.text: $m$ identical balls are to be placed in $n$ distinct bags. You are given that $m\ge kn$, where $k$ is a natural number $\ge1$. In how many ways can the balls be placed in the bags if each bag must contain at least $k$ balls?

Consider the following logic program $P$:
$$\begin{array}{l}A(x)\leftarrow B(x,y),C(y)\\ \leftarrow B(x,x)\end{array}$$
Which of the following first order sentences is equivalent to $P$?
questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.referenceAnswer: The rule says that for every x and y, B(x,y) and C(y) imply A(x). Because A does not depend on y, this is equivalent to requiring A(x) whenever some y satisfies the conjunction. The empty-head clause forbids B(x,x) for every x, giving not-exists x B(x,x). Conjoin the two conditions: A.

questions.text:
A processor uses 2-level page tables for virtual to physical address translation. Page tables for both levels are stored in the main memory. Virtual and physical addresses are both 32 bits wide. The memory is byte addressable. For virtual to physical address translation, the 10 most significant bits of the virtual address are used as index into the first level page table while the next 10 bits are used as index into the second level page table. The 12 least significant bits of the virtual address are used as offset within the page. Assume that the page table entries in both levels of page tables are 4 bytes wide. Further, the processor has a translation look-aside buffer (TLB), with a hit rate of 96%. The TLB caches recently used virtual page numbers and the corresponding physical page numbers. The processor also has a physically addressed cache with a hit ratio of 90%. Main memory access time is 10 ns, cache access time is 1 ns, and TLB access time is also 1 ns.
Assuming that no page faults occur, the average time taken to access a virtual address is approximately (to the nearest 0.5 ns)
questions.subject: 5. Operating Systems
questions.referenceAnswer: The serial lookup model gives data access $0.9(1)+0.1(1+10)=2$ ns. TLB costs 1 ns. A TLB miss (probability .04) additionally reads two page-table entries at 10 ns each. Thus $1+2+0.04(20)=3.8$ ns, rounded to the nearest 0.5 ns gives 4 ns. If a failed cache lookup is overlapped with memory, 3.7 ns still rounds to 3.5, so the serial model matters; the printed question is interpreted using separate lookup costs.
